nodes.note: c1 finds the latest release tag with git describe.
c2 lists the commits since the tag with git log.
The skill never checks whether there are any commits since the tag.
There is no end state for reporting that there is nothing to release.
k2 and c9 handle the BREAKING CHANGE fork and make major take priority.
c9 bumps the major version on a breaking change.
k1 with c7 and c8 handles the feat: fork with both branches.
c7 bumps the minor version when there is a feat: commit.
c8 bumps the patch version otherwise.
c10 puts the Breaking changes section first but asks for no migration notes for users.
c3 to c5 group commits into Features, Bug fixes and Other, and c6 leaves out chore: commits.
The skill never credits commit authors, and its git log format leaves out the author.
c11 writes RELEASE_NOTES.md headed with ## v<version>.
The skill does not say the notes are ready for review or hand them off.
c12 and c13 forbid creating tags and pushing.
c2 prints short hashes, but nothing tells the agent to link each entry to its commit.

rule-never-create-git-tags.text: Never create git tags or push; release managers publish the release.

rule-link-every-entry-to.note: c2 prints short hashes, but nothing tells the agent to link each entry to its commit.
rule-link-every-entry-to.text: Link every entry to its commit hash.

findings.message: The skill never asks for any: 'Are there any commits since the tag?'.
The skill never asks for credit: "Credit each commit's author".
The skill never asks for rule-link-every-entry-to: 'Link every entry to its commit hash.'.
The skill never says what to do when any is 'no'.
migration is only partly covered by c10. c10 puts the Breaking changes section first but asks for no migration notes for users.
